title: Fuel Cell Arrangements
story:
The drone bay can line up its fuel cells in `n!` (n factorial) different orders: `n × (n − 1) × … × 1`, and `0!` is 1. SIGMA wants the count.

Input: one whole number `n` (0–20).

Output: `n!`.

Example: `5` prints `120`.

Careful: the answer gets very large very fast.
hints: Multiply 1 × 2 × … × n in a loop, or recursively: `n! = n × (n − 1)!` with `0! = 1`.
An `int` only goes up to about 2 billion; 13! is over 6 billion. Hidden tests go up to 20!.
Use `long long` for the result and print it with `%lld`.
